summary: Obfuscated payload compiled and executed on import in @adminide-stack/yantra-help-browser
details: lib/index.js, the package main entry point, contains a custom permutation-cipher decoder (`spin`/`peel`, keyed by two numeric constant arrays NX/SX) that reconstructs an approximately 15 KB scrambled string literal into JavaScript source. The decoded source is then compiled via `peel.constructor` (which resolves to the `Function` constructor) and immediately invoked with `global` and `require` as arguments. This bootstrap runs whenever a consumer `require`s or `import`s the package. Handing `require` to a dynamically compiled, obfuscated payload grants it full Node capability (filesystem, network, child_process) on the installing/importing host. The package's declared purpose is a React help-browser feature; the companion `module.js` is clean, with the obfuscated loader appended to the main export, consistent with a smuggled payload grafted onto an otherwise legitimate module. The combination of a bespoke custom decoder, a hidden ~15 KB string literal, and runtime `Function()` compilation with `require` passed in is the canonical shape of an import-time dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
